system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience role. I am
an early-career developer with hands-on experience building React interfaces, improving
accessibility, and writing automated unit tests. Verdane Care’s focus on patient-first,
straightforward healthcare experiences strongly appeals to me, particularly its commitment to
accessibility and privacy by default.
During my software development internship at Harbourline Media, I worked on the company’s
React news site and resolved accessibility issues across more than 20 components, including
keyboard navigation, colour contrast, and ARIA labels. I also built a reusable image gallery
component with Storybook stories and wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.
These experiences have given me a practical foundation in accessible interface development,
reusable components, Storybook, and automated unit testing.
My academic and project experience complements this work: I earned a First Class Honours
degree in Computing – Software Development, and built Tidewatch, an accessible tide and
weather app, using React, TypeScript, and Node.js. I have also built a booking website for a
local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, giving me additional experience with a
wellness-related user journey. My academic project used React, TypeScript, and Node.js, and
my technical skills also include Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, Git and GitHub, and WCAG 2.1
accessibility. I would bring a thoughtful, user-focused approach to building patient-facing
features, with a particular interest in Verdane Care’s privacy-by-default approach.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
experience and interest in accessible, straightforward web experiences could contribute to
Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team. As a native English speaker, I would be comfortable
collaborating.
Kind regards,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
